rows.notes: Mean (SE) 207.4 (9.1), marked double-dagger = p<0.001 vs placebo; n=25; median 191.0 (Q1,Q3 180.0, 227.0); min-max 147.0-306.0. Graded 1: statistically significant but clinically non-actionable - the mean, the Q1 and even the group MINIMUM (147.0) all sit above the stated human LLN of 140 K/mm3 (Figure 4 legend). -10.3% vs placebo is a derived ratio. This is the largest human mean platelet decrement in the dataset and the human counterpart of the NHP high-dose effect; it produced ZERO <75 K/mm3 events in the same dose band (Table 2), which is the article's central animal-to-human translation point: 'NHPs may over predict the propensity of 2'MOE chimeric ASOs to reduce platelets in humans.' The >275-375 mg column is empty at Dose 6 (cell did not meet n>=10 / >=4 ASOs).

rows.notes: ADJACENT / CONTEXT ROW, is_platelet_specific=FALSE because the statement is ALL-CAUSE, not platelet-specific; it entails but does not separately report zero platelet-driven discontinuations. Table 3 values: 6068 study samples screened; 65 potentially positive samples; 35 patients with at least 1 positive time point at SCREENING; 1 patient with at least 1 CONFIRMED positive time point; 2 samples confirmed positive; titer 50 (1:50). INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE SOURCE: the Results text says the 65 potentially positive samples were 'collected from 39 patients', whereas Table 3 gives 35 patients with at least one positive screening time point. rows.notes: MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE — grade 0. A production-side (megakaryocyte) mechanism was excluded, pointing to peripheral platelet clearance instead. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: this is a bare assertion in the Discussion; the paper describes NO assay, criteria, bone-marrow examination or supporting data for the exclusion and cites no reference for it, so readout_value is the qualitative word 'excluded' and effect_vs_control is TBD. tissue is recorded as bone_marrow because that is the compartment the claim concerns, but no bone-marrow sampling is reported. CONVERGENCE ACROSS SOURCES: this agrees with the independent EMA EPAR finding of no haematopoietic/bone-marrow toxicity in cynomolgus monkeys, so two independent documents concur that the mechanism is peripheral rather than central — a useful human-to-animal extrapolation anchor.

rows.system_model: patient_cohort (APPROACH phase 3 RCT, NCT02211209, familial chylomicronemia syndrome)
rows.source_table: Discussion, p540-541 narrative ('Nearly all the patients received an injection of heparin at the beginning of the trial and at approximately 26 weeks to enable measurement of LPL activity, but a classic heparin-induced mechanism for thrombocytopenia was excluded')
rows.notes: MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE — grade 0, and an important confounder-exclusion specific to this trial. Nearly all patients received heparin TWICE (at baseline and ~week 26) because post-heparin LPL activity was an eligibility/assessment measure, creating a genuine risk that heparin-induced thrombocytopenia would be mistaken for drug-induced thrombocytopenia; the authors state classic HIT was excluded. LIMITATION: no anti-PF4/heparin antibody assay, 4T score, timing analysis or other criteria are described and no data are shown, so readout_value is the qualitative word 'excluded'. Recorded because ruling out HIT is what licenses attributing the platelet signal to the oligonucleotide itself. Note that PF4 is the antigen in classic HIT and PS-oligonucleotide/PF4 interaction is a known mechanism of interest for this endpoint, but this paper does not address that possibility.

rows.system_model: patient_cohort (APPROACH phase 3 RCT, NCT02211209, familial chylomicronemia syndrome, patients with the most severe events)
rows.source_table: Discussion, p540-541 narrative ('The underlying mechanisms responsible for the declines in platelet levels are not clear at present... There was some evidence for associated immunologic response in the most severe events')
rows.notes: QUALITATIVE MECHANISTIC ROW, graded 3 on the severity of the events it refers to (the CTCAE grade-4 cases). GRADING CAVEAT STATED EXPLICITLY: this does NOT satisfy the rubric's 'immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with CONFIRMED anti-platelet antibodies' criterion, because NO anti-platelet antibody result of any kind is reported anywhere in this paper — the authors say only that there was 'some evidence for associated immunologic response', with no assay, titre, numbers or reference given, and they state plainly that the underlying mechanism 'is not clear at present'. readout_value therefore carries the source's hedged wording verbatim and effect_vs_control is TBD. This is the strongest support this paper offers for the rare, severe, immune-mediated limb of the endpoint's bimodal presentation, and it is weak; the two grade-4 patients' clinical response to glucocorticoids and IVIG is circumstantially consistent with an immune mechanism but is not presented as evidence by the authors. FOR CONTRAST, the EMA EPAR reports that anti-drug-antibody status did NOT increase the incidence of platelet decrease (78% ADA-negative vs 38% ADA-positive) and that anti-platelet antibodies were undetectable in 7 of 8 affected monkeys — both arguing against an antibody-mediated mechanism.
